_comment: Shared trust-evaluation vectors. Both the Node and the Dart directory
cache verifiers must return `expect` for each `directory`. Regenerate with

cases.name: grandfathered_roots_accepted
cases.why: A policy signed by a trusted App, with every root grandfathered, is the ordinary case.

cases.name: policy_signer_revoked_after_signing
cases.why: A signature does not stop verifying because the signer was revoked later; only the signer's window at signing time matters.

cases.name: policy_signer_revoked_before_signing
cases.why: A signer that was already revoked when it signed the policy carries no weight.

cases.name: policy_signer_approved_after_signing
cases.why: A signer that had not yet been vouched for when it signed cannot authorize a policy.

cases.name: policy_signature_forged
cases.why: The approver's signature is what makes the policy a policy; a tampered body must not verify.

cases.name: admission_signed_inside_rotation_window
cases.why: A key that signed while it was still the device's current one keeps its approvals.

cases.name: policy_signer_rotated_after_signing
cases.why: Rotating a signing device's key leaves its old key as chain history with no approval timestamp; the signature it made while current still stands.

cases.name: admission_signed_after_rotation
cases.why: A superseded key keeps its signature forever, so without a window check it could keep admitting devices long after the device rotated past it.

cases.name: admitted_by_revoked_grandfathered_root
cases.why: Skipping a revoked root keeps the rest of the directory usable, but the root must then anchor nothing — the device it admitted no longer resolves to a live root.

cases.name: admitted_by_live_grandfathered_root
cases.why: The counterpart: an admission from a root that is still trusted resolves, and its device joins the directory.

cases.name: grandfathered_key_anchors_rotated_device
cases.why: Rotation is not a new device: the snapshot names the pre-rotation key, and that key still anchors the device through its current head.

cases.name: reapproved_grandfathered_root
cases.why: Removing and re-approving a device returns the same key, so it resolves through the snapshot it was always in.

cases.name: one_revoked_root_among_live_ones
cases.why: A revoked root contributes nothing but must not disturb the roots around it.

cases.name: grandfathered_key_absent_from_directory
cases.why: A root the directory no longer carries is skipped, not treated as a policy failure.

cases.name: pending_device_alongside_live_roots
cases.why: A device awaiting approval is neither authorized nor unresolved.

cases.name: policy_disabled_needs_no_proof
cases.why: With the gate off there is no admission graph to evaluate.

cases.name: policy_reset_to_unsigned
cases.why: An epoch reset clears the proof and the gate together; nothing is left to verify.

cases.name: admitted_by_app_that_then_rotated
cases.why: An approval made while the App's key was current survives that App rotating afterwards.

cases.name: admitted_then_approver_removed
cases.why: An admission only counts while its approver is still an authorized root, so removing the App strands the device it admitted.
